title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has issued a response to a 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans to address the recommendations made. The government aims to promote trust and safety in AI systems through regulation and collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

title: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education
description: The Department for Education’s (DfE) position on the use of generative AI in the education sector.
summary: The UK Department for Education (DfE) policy outlines its stance on the use of generative AI in educational settings, aiming to provide guidance and oversight. This policy will likely address the role, benefits, and potential risks of generative AI in educational environments.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: This document outlines Ofqual's approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications. The policy aims to address concerns around AI use in exams and assessment, following requests from government ministers.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This policy document is a report and assessment on the use of copyrighted works in the development of artificial intelligence systems, and it aims to understand the impact of this use on copyright law and society as a whole. It likely examines the implications of AI systems relying on copyrighted materials for their operation and suggests potential solutions or regulations to address these issues.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to a report from the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, highlighting the importance of addressing potential risks associated with AI technologies. The response aims to ensure the UK's AI development balances benefits with necessary safety measures.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the terms of reference for a review into the intersection of artificial intelligence and public standards, aiming to establish guidelines and standards for the use of AI in public contexts. It also provides frequently asked questions to address potential concerns and clarify the review's objectives and scope.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The Cabinet Office's Committee on Standards in Public Life (CSPL) has shared its perspectives on the governance of artificial intelligence. This submission aims to inform the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry into the governance of AI.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This AI policy document discusses how AI will affect regulations for medical products, and aims to implement the principles outlined in the AI White Paper. The document will help establish guidelines for the safe use of AI in the medical product industry.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the UK defence organization the most effective, efficient, and trusted in the world when it comes to AI. It outlines a vision for the organization to be a leader in the field of artificial intelligence in defence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: This is a government plan outlining how to utilize artificial intelligence in the transport sector while addressing its risks. It aims to work with the industry to benefit from AI advancements.
